about: Shared, sourced fact bank for the Dad ticker and the Simmie terminal. Each fact checked against its source page on 2026-10-23. Age filter: age_min <= dial age <= age_max.

facts.text: A day on Venus, 243 Earth days, is longer than its year of 225 Earth days.
On Venus the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east, because Venus spins the other way.
Venus is hotter than Mercury, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.
Venus has no moon, but it has a companion asteroid called Zoozve, a name that began as a misread poster label.
Sunlight takes about eight minutes to reach Earth, and about six to reach Venus.
Saturn is the only planet whose average density is less than water's.
The Moon moves about an inch, roughly 2.5 cm, farther from Earth each year.
We only ever see one side of the Moon, because it spins at the same rate it circles Earth.
No one saw the far side of the Moon until a spacecraft flew past it in 1959.
Apollo astronauts brought 382 kilograms of Moon rock and soil back to Earth.
Jupiter holds more than twice the material of every other planet, moon and asteroid combined.
Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a storm bigger than Earth that has lasted for hundreds of years.
Olympus Mons on Mars is about 40 km tall from base to summit. Everest is 8.8 km.
A day on Mars lasts 24.6 hours, very close to a day on Earth.
Sunlight takes about 13 minutes to reach Mars.
One full day-night cycle on Mercury lasts 176 Earth days, just over two Mercury years.
Uranus is tipped at nearly 90 degrees, so it rolls around the Sun like a ball.
Neptune was the first planet found by mathematical prediction rather than by looking.
Neptune is the only planet in our solar system you can't see with the naked eye.
One lap of the Sun takes Neptune 165 years. It finished its first since discovery in 2011.
The space station circles Earth 16 times a day, so its crew passes through 16 sunrises and sunsets.
A sugar cube of neutron star material would weigh about a billion tonnes on Earth, about as much as a mountain.
The Andromeda Galaxy, our nearest large neighbour, is 2.5 million light-years away.
The Sun holds 99.8% of all the mass in our solar system.
Earth is the only planet whose English name doesn't come from Greek or Roman myths.
A year is about 365.25 days. The extra quarter day is why we add a leap day every four years.
Pluto's moon Charon is about half Pluto's size, the largest moon for its planet's size in the solar system.
Pluto was discovered in 1930 and reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
Titan is the only world besides Earth known to have rivers, lakes and seas on its surface, of liquid methane and ethane.
Saturn's moon Titan is bigger than the planet Mercury.
Some comets from the distant Oort Cloud take as long as 30 million years to orbit the Sun once.
Platypuses and echidnas are monotremes, mammals that lay eggs.
Male platypuses have a venom spur on each ankle, making them one of the few venomous mammals.
Blue whales are the largest animals ever known to have lived on Earth.
Blue whale calls may carry to other whales up to about 1,600 km away.
Blue whales are estimated to live around 80 to 90 years.
A newborn blue whale calf weighs about 2.5 tonnes.
Some humpback whales swim about 8,000 km between their breeding and feeding grounds.
Every humpback's tail markings are unique, so scientists can recognise individuals from photos.
About 80% of a superb lyrebird's song is mimicry. It can copy chainsaws and car engines.
Wombats are among the world's largest burrowing animals.
Emperor penguins are the only animals that breed during the Antarctic winter.
The emperor is the largest of the 18 penguin species.
A red kangaroo joey leaves the pouch for good at around 235 days old.
Female Antarctic krill can lay up to 10,000 eggs at a time.
Babies have about 300 bones. They gradually fuse into the 206 bones adults have.
Your lower jawbone is the only bone in your head you can move.
The stirrup bone behind your eardrum is only about 3 mm long.
Your spine is made of 33 bones.
Your heart pumps blood to every cell in your body in less than a minute.
You have more than 600 muscles.
Each of your eyes has about 120 million rods and 7 million cones.
You get 20 baby teeth, then 32 permanent ones.
Lightning can heat the air to about five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
Helium was found in the Sun's light during an 1868 eclipse, years before it was found on Earth.
Diamond and graphite are both forms of pure carbon.
In 1694, scientists focused sunlight on a diamond with a large magnifying glass, and it slowly disappeared.
Australian Wi-Fi technology developed at CSIRO is in more than 15 billion devices.
CSIRO's Wi-Fi breakthrough drew on what its team had learned about radio waves from radio astronomy.
The first prototype computer mouse had a wooden case.
The word 'mouse' doesn't appear in Engelbart's patent for the device.
Great Basin bristlecone pines grow only in California, Nevada and Utah, and some are thousands of years old.
Pando, an aspen grove in Utah's Wasatch Mountains, is estimated to be around 16,000 years old.
Only about 0.4% of Antarctica isn't covered by ice.
Antarctica's ice sheet is 2.16 km thick on average.
The Lambert Glacier in Antarctica is the world's largest glacier, about 400 km long.
